# Strain — source-qualified playtest reference

**Status: REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the supplied namespace, penalty and recovery scope.** [GPT's exact disposition](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_FINAL_REVIEW.md) confirms this bounded candidate. The two names below refer to independent systems. This candidate preserves the Warrior engine and retains the Gameplay Loop's expedition track as a provisional campaign overlay. It does not promote that older table into the approved Core book.

Use [source bindings](../../data/playtest/strain_bindings.json), [source validation](STRAIN_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [combat timing](COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md), [conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md) and [HP/Wounds](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). The [first GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_FIRST_REVIEW.md) and [counterexample corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_COUNTEREXAMPLE_REVIEW.md) preserve the decisions. The latter corrects an earlier summary that misplaced the expedition attack/save penalties at level3; their source places them at level2.

## Identify the track first

| Mechanical ID | What it represents | Range | Generic recovery |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `warrior.serum-strain` | The Warrior serum/mutation engine, including an explicit Serum Sharing recipient | 0–3 | Beneficial completed1h Short Rest−1; beneficial completed8h Long Rest→0 |
| `expedition.strain` | Campaign attrition, Rest Debt, unsupported Supply, Quickglass crash and ordinary Wound-treatment critical failure | 0–6 | Secure beneficial Long Rest−1 eligible point; Morale Rest−1; qualifying Haven care removes all eligible ordinary points |

Neither is global `core.exhaustion`, Oracle Revelation backlash, Dissonance or historical Resonance Burn. A single cause applies multiple tracks only if its operative source explicitly says so. Serum3 never becomes expedition3, and serum overflow never becomes expedition6. A namespace binding identifies a reference; it does not itself apply any effect.

Inside the supplied Warrior engine/cards, Strain means serum Strain. In the supplied campaign references, Strain means expedition Strain. **Future ambiguous sources remain unbound until reviewed.** The source register records8 Warrior engine references,17 cards,3 campaign sections and12 exact Core paragraphs. Do not classify a new immunity or source by its name alone.

Quickglass's crash adds1 expedition point and retains its independent one-hour DEX-check disadvantage. Ordinary Wound-treatment Critical Failure adds1 expedition point to the **patient**, without inventing another Wound or Exhaustion level. Morale Rest removes expedition Strain only. Serum Tolerance suppresses the profile side effects it names; it does not prevent serum Strain or its penalties.

## Warrior serum Strain

Preserve the source engine: normal Serum Injection/Mutagen Injection and Mutation Surge add1; Serum Cocktail/Mutation Overload add2 unless a printed modifier applies. Cap3. At2, Speed−5. At3, also AC−1 and saves−1; the source's voluntary serum/Cocktail/Overclock/Surge activation lock applies. All card costs, prepared doses, mutation limits and frequencies remain required.

For an activation explicitly illegal if it exceeds the cap, calculate its **final modified gain first**, including applicable Mutation Adaptation and the minimum1 for Cocktail/Overload where applicable. Reject a resulting value above3. Never clip a voluntary overcap cost into legality. A separate activation lock can still prohibit activation even if a gain modifier makes its cost small or zero.

Automatic later gains, such as the actual **Sanguine Surge** profile's ending side effect, clamp at3. They do not retroactively invalidate the original activation, cause overflow death or add expedition points.

**Serum Sharing — NEW integration.** Its willing recipient receives serum Strain even when not a Warrior. At recipient3, the attempted+1 clamps at3; this is not the recipient activating an otherwise locked class ability. The recipient retains all existing penalties and receives only the card's actual diluted effects and side effects. Source-owner Serum Tolerance does not protect the ally. Recipient Strain uses the same beneficial1h/8h recovery; no serum preparation, mutation slots or other Warrior powers are granted.

## Expedition Strain

NEW interpretation: rows are cumulative. Preserve the original placement of effects:

| Level | Additional consequence |
|---:|---|
| 0 | None |
| 1 | −1 initiative and expedition checks |
| 2 | Speed−10; −1 attacks and saving throws |
| 3 | Disadvantage on expedition checks; Dash lock below |
| 4 | Effective maximum HP×3/4 |
| 5 | Core Incapacitated plus the explicit movement restriction below |
| 6 | Deterministic death/collapse endpoint below |

Initiative−1 applies when a roll is made. Changing Strain does not reorder an established encounter. Ordinary advantage/disadvantage does not numerically stack from multiple sources.

Represent each point with `pointId`, `sourceId`, `ordinaryRemovable` and `removalGateMet`. Level is the active count, maximum6. Keep source history and attempted overflow even when no additional point can be stored. A generic recovery can select only points that are ordinary-removable **and** whose gate is met. A specific treatment can override only the source it expressly covers. Clearing a gate updates metadata; it does not silently delete a point.

**Level6 — NEW deterministic interpretation.** On every positive, unprevented expedition gain that would reach **or exceed6**, evaluate that gain's endpoint before clamping stored points at6. Default: ordinary Dead state. Only that gain's explicit reviewed nonlethal source can instead produce `expedition.collapse`. A living collapsed creature already at6 can die from a later ordinary gain; it is not protected by the cap. A prevented/zero gain causes no endpoint. Nonlethal gains or Strain removal never revive a corpse.

Collapse leaves the creature alive, Unconscious, Speed0 and unable to act/travel. It does not set HP0, grant Stable or create death saves by itself. Independently dying0HP creatures still follow their normal saves. Short/Long/Morale Rest cannot reduce expedition points while this level6 collapse persists; qualifying24h Haven care or explicit treatment may. Collapse ends only when the track falls below6. Other Unconscious sources remain independent. If all six points stay blocked, Haven care cannot clear the collapse by assertion.

This recoverable collapse is a **NEW operational replacement** for the source's undefined “permanent collapse” alternative. The original wording remains preserved; it did not itself specify this recovery. Actual resurrection while six expedition points remain is a separate unresolved resurrection interface.

## Independent penalties and maximum HP

Apply flat Speed changes first, floor at0, then applicable multipliers and floor normally. A rule setting Speed0 takes precedence. Serum2's−5 and expedition2's−10 coexist: base30 becomes15, then Exhaustion2's half Speed gives7. Mutation Adaptation's explicit serum Speed exception does not cancel expedition Speed loss.

Expedition2 and serum3 each impose saves−1, totaling−2. The class rule against stacking duplicate bonuses does not merge these independent tracks.

NEW maximum-HP composition: multiply applicable rational factors against the same otherwise-applicable maximum, floor **once**, minimum1. Expedition4×3/4 and Exhaustion4×1/2 produce37 from base100. Clamp currentHP down if necessary; that clamp is not damage and triggers no Wound, death-save failure or damage resource. Removing a modifier raises capacity without healing/resetting death counters. Critical Wounds' healing ceiling then uses `max(1, effectiveMaximumHP−1)`; it is not another maxHP multiplier.

The helper accepts other multipliers only after their compatibility has been established elsewhere. It does not decide whether unrelated gear/ancestry/spell modifiers stack.

## Dash lock — NEW

At expedition3–4, a legal Dash consumes the current opportunity and creates a lock. No other Dash is legal while locked, whether Action, Bonus Action, extra Action or extra turn. A non-Dash Action, round boundary or extra turn does not clear it.

In initiative, lock through the **end of the next future regular turn** of the creature. A Dash during its current turn excludes that current end, using the exact marker-exclusion rule from combat. Thus turn1 Dash blocks another that turn and turn2; turn2's end unlocks turn3. An off-turn Dash locks through the next regular turn's end. Extra turns cannot substitute for that marker.

Outside initiative, unlock at Dash time+6 seconds. Preserve whichever endpoint was recorded across initiative entry/exit/reorder; do not restart or convert it. Falling below expedition3 clears the restriction and stored lock immediately. Returning to3 begins unlocked until a new legal Dash. Expedition5 cannot Dash at all.

The exact review confirms exclusion of the current in-progress turn end. Its earlier “strictly after Dash” shorthand is superseded by these specific marker rules and tests.

## Expedition5 and assistance

Core Incapacitated denies Action/Bonus Action/Reaction and ends concentration. NEW expedition-specific restriction: no voluntary tactical movement in initiative. This does **not** redefine generic Incapacitated or automatically set the creature's actual Speed statistic to0. Forced movement, an external legal teleport and lawful carrying still work.

Outside combat, apply the slow-travel exception by halving the otherwise legal walking/travel pace once after applicable load/Speed/environment rules. Do not repeatedly halve per Watch or invent miles-per-hour values here. Detailed stacking with other travel-pace modifiers remains the travel review's responsibility.

Brief communication is possible if no other condition prevents it. The victim cannot use an Action-time consumable by itself. A legal willing recipient can be fed, given a potion or treated by someone paying the actual required Action/activity, supplies and costs. This creates no free administration or universal restraint/capture rule. Rest and Haven care remain possible when their eligibility requirements are met.

## Recovery and actual elapsed time

Preserve campaign limits: Short Rest1h, at most **two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests**; Long Rest8h, at most **one beneficial Long Rest per24 elapsed hours**. Those limits apply to serum recovery too, including non-Warrior recipients. Exact completion timestamps and IDs prevent replay. Work, travel, short rest, sleep and recreation cannot spend the same active hours twice. Unfinished/interrupted activity provides no completion benefit.

**Rest Debt order.** First complete a qualifying safe8hRestWatch and clear debt it satisfies. Then evaluate beneficial Long Rest eligibility. If eligible, apply its sourced benefits, including serum reset and one eligible expedition point when secure. Persistent food/water/source blocks still prevent expedition reduction. An additional safe RestWatch inside the24h reward cap can discharge debt but cannot restore resources, remove expedition Strain, reset the beneficial-rest clock or reset short-rest counts.

**Secure Long Rest.** Remove one eligible expedition point chosen by the patient, once the rest qualifies and no reduction block remains. This is a separate benefit from serum reset, so one actual qualifying rest may do both. Class-only serum reduction never silently removes expedition points.

**Morale Rest — NEW endpoint.** Four consecutive safe hours of voluntarily chosen recreation, without forced substance use, work, expedition travel or simultaneous sleep/ShortRest. At most one beneficial Morale Rest per24 elapsed hours. Remove one eligible expedition point. It never removes a Wound. A distinct4hMoraleRest plus an eligible8hsecureLongRest can legitimately remove two points; there is no new shared one-point cap.

**Haven care.** One full day means24 consecutive hours under qualifying Haven care/location conditions, with real care, food and water supplied under campaign rules. One active care interval per patient; interrupted care gives no completion benefit and restarting requires a fresh24h window. At completion remove all eligible ordinary expedition points; blocked/special points remain. The care window may contain separate sleep, meals and4h recreation because it is not24h of active practitioner work. Incompatible practitioner activities cannot be double-counted.

The Strain reference does not replace HP/RP/RC rest rewards or settle all supply prices, travel limits or camp security. Those systems retain their source review gates.

## Immunity, suppression and removal

Only explicit source-qualified wording changes a track. Poison immunity, global Exhaustion immunity, serum-profile tolerance and expedition immunity do not automatically cover serum Strain. Exhaustion removal does not clear either track. An unqualified future “immune to Strain” remains unbound.

- “Cannot gain expedition Strain” blocks gains only.
- “Ignore expedition Strain penalties” retains the points; no implied prevention of gain or level6 endpoint.
- “Remove X expedition Strain” actually removes eligible points under that source.

These tracks do not inherit the generic condition-immunity suppression rule merely because their UI label resembles a condition.

## Reference scope

The implementation in `tools/strain_playtest_rules.py` covers selected namespace lookups, gain/cap/death transitions, point recovery, numeric composition, Dash deadlines and completed-rest accounting. It does not run the campaign, grant class abilities, create inventory, verify all care activities, dispatch conditions or perform resurrection. The caller supplies legality and source eligibility. Its penalty projection does not replace independent life-state, collapse, condition or travel rules.

The namespace lookup rejects unknown/ambiguous sources. Low-level transition helpers such as `expedition_gain` accept already-validated source IDs from their caller; they do not independently repeat the registry lookup.

The [validation report](STRAIN_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) records71 transition checks,30 exact source checks and4,949 maximum-HP invariant states. Broader rest rewards, travel, all-source class semantics, future Strain references, resurrection and human balance remain open.

# Enchantment control integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. These NEW integration rules accompany seven approved rank-two Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK2_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted body and records the binding interpretations below. Source originals remain preserved. This is not runtime certification, human balance approval, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery approval.

## Ordinary compelled Attack Actions

When an actual compulsion orders an ordinary Attack Action, use the target's native ordinary attack sequence, including inherent Extra Attack and an NPC's native Multiattack if that is actually its ordinary Action. No additional Action/attack is granted. A source expressly limited to one attack retains that limit: Confusing Flash is such an exception. An ordinary attack instruction is not permission to invent an Attack Action or convert another source's single attack into Multiattack.

Spend required ordinary ammunition normally. The command cannot activate consumable magic, special ammunition with a distinct expendable feature, RP/spellcasting, charges, recharge/per-rest abilities or optional finite-resource riders. Actual optional expenditures remain optional and cannot be compelled indirectly by choosing a method which requires them. Where instruction wording leaves the choice open, the target/controller may use a different legal ordinary method. If none satisfies the instruction, that instruction fails without spending a prohibited resource or manufacturing one. Existing source-specific limits and actual absolute prohibitions remain.

## Application IDs and independently scoped components

Each cast has a distinct application ID. Each component retains its own exact source/caster/target, application identity, deadline and actual defense state. Replacing one component never silently replaces another.

For Dire Charm, successfully established Charmed replaces only that caster's previous Dire Charm Charmed relation. Successfully established servant control replaces only the existing Dire Charm servant component across casters. Charmed-only and servant-only casts can therefore coexist. A successful repeat save, expiry or removal clears only still-active components originating from that application; an old application's save cannot remove a replacement component from another cast. Empty applications have no remaining save schedule. Core Charmed from other sources is unaffected. Shared hard-control history never refunds, even if a component is suppressed or replaced before acting.

## Compelled budget arbitration

This NEW rule resolves collisions among actual active mandatory instructions, including Command, Confusing Flash, Illusive Commands, Dire Charm and Crown of Madness. It does not create commands, extend duration, add repeated control to a one-turn source, grant new target permissions or override an explicit source-specific exception.

Record a priority timestamp for each specific instruction:
- Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands: successful establishment of that failed-save instruction.
- Dire Charm and Crown of Madness: issue of that turn's particular valid order, not the age of the underlying spell alone.
- Simultaneous instructions: underlying effect application order, then a stable source/mechanical ID as the neutral tie-break. Record it before resolving choices; do not decide a favorable order after outcomes.

At execution, gather still-active mandatory instructions and consider earlier priority first. A currently impossible/ineligible instruction claims no budget; proceed to the next. Compatible requirements can share one genuine legal execution. A single Action satisfies two instructions only if that same Action actually fulfills both. Once an earlier valid instruction claims an indivisible ordinary Action/interaction, an incompatible later instruction receives no second copy. Movement uses only the actual remaining movement allowance; sequencing instructions cannot reset spent movement or violate an earlier still-maintained posture/restriction.

A losing ongoing instruction is ineffective only for its contested budget/opportunity, not automatically dispelled. Its compatible independent portions may still operate within existing permissions. Its own endpoint, replacement and saves remain. Priority loss never refunds hard-control history. An invalid later order cannot erase an earlier mandate merely by being issued.

Example: Grovel and an Attack Action may both be satisfied if Prone uses only legal movement/posture and the attack remains legal. Two incompatible ordinary Actions cannot both be demanded from one Action budget. This arbitrates actual compelled behavior; it does not make compulsion optional or restore unavailable actions.

## Six-second control cadence outside initiative

This NEW cadence binds Dire Charm and Crown of Madness's ongoing order/end-save procedures. Other sources retain their actual timing unless expressly bound by a further review.

For a target with no existing initiative/control cycle, successful outside-initiative application begins a six-second virtual target cycle: first START immediately after resolution, first END six elapsed seconds later, then repeated six-second cycles. END resolves before the next cycle's START at the same boundary. Maximum duration remains the original absolute60-second deadline; expiry can end the spell before a later opportunity.

Reviewed procedure: a target shares one active virtual control cycle and one ordinary behavior budget across concurrent control applications. A new application during an already-open virtual cycle does not replay START or replenish budgets; its specifically allowed current-cycle END save still occurs. Each spell retains its own maximum deadline, components and saves. This treats application during an outside-initiative cycle like application during an existing regular turn, preventing repeated casts from creating extra immediate Actions.

The cycle supplies the bound spells' order opportunities, one ordinary six-second behavior budget where needed, and their repeat saves. It does not refresh encounter Reactions, recharge, resources, limited uses or manufacture extra combat turns. If actual combat order becomes necessary, establish ordinary initiative before any not-yet-committed hostile behavior; a virtual cycle is no permission for an extra pre-initiative attack.

Reviewed procedure for entering initiative: map the currently open virtual cycle to the target's first actual regular turn. Carry already received order opportunities and spent ordinary Action/movement/interaction budgets into that turn; do not replay or refill them at its START. The next still-unresolved END save occurs at that actual turn's END. Thereafter use actual regular starts/ends for future triggers. Keep the original absolute duration deadline. Do not replay already resolved virtual events. Existing effects begun in initiative retain their ordinary original virtual-marker rules if they later leave it; this bridge is for these effects first established outside initiative.

Application after an actual regular START grants no order for that already-started turn. A source explicitly permitting an affected current-turn END save still grants that save. Extra turns do not add order opportunities or repeat saves.

## Fixed-zone eligibility history

Calm Emotions and Zone of Truth have fixed spherical centers and require actual exposure/line of effect from that center. Geometric presence behind total cover is not yet eligible exposure. When cover opens around a creature still inside, that moment counts as its first eligible exposure.

Keep one save/acceptance result per creature per spell application:
- Calm Emotions: willing acceptance or the actual WIS save at first eligible exposure.
- Zone of Truth: the actual CHA save at first eligible exposure.
- Success: unaffected by that cast for its remainder, including later entry/cover changes.
- Acceptance/failure: the cast's existing effect is active only while exposed inside its zone; leaving or total cover suppresses it, and restored exposure resumes it without another save.

Acceptance is not a freely toggled dispel choice. Independent zones retain separate casters, concentration, histories and deadlines. Identical restrictions or suppression do not add numerical magnitude. Being unaffected by one zone does not make a creature immune to a different cast.

Calm Emotions suppresses actual Frightened effects, including a newly acquired Frightened source. Create and retain underlying records, ordinary clocks, maintenance and scheduled repeat saves. Once no valid suppressor remains, still-existing effects resume without replaying their original application. A condition which independently expires or is cured while suppressed does not return.

No emotion-themed name automatically disables a class ability. Actual Mooncursed, Momentum Rampage, Divine Fury, Fury of the Host and Beast Empathy source cards have no new emotion-maintenance requirement here. Their real Frightened rider on an affected recipient remains subject to suppression; other printed effects continue.

## Scope and open evidence

The instruction-priority, split-component and zone histories above are authored tabletop procedures, not executed stateful engine implementations. Concurrent outside-initiative applications and the first real turn's carried budget have exact manuscript approval; executable runtime integration remains open. Human testing remains necessary for multiple-attack compulsion, long control without concentration, fear suppression and the unchanged Zone of Truth class-price discrepancy.

## Binding interpretations from the exact review

One-shot Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands do not gain a new repeating cadence from this overlay. If their compelled behavior falls into the same current six-second/regular-turn opportunity, their demands compete for the same actual remaining behavior budget through Compelled Budget Arbitration.

Ordinary actual regular-start processing still happens at the first real regular turn: Reaction refresh, recharge, death-save and start effects follow their normal combat rules. Only the Enchantment control START/order opportunity and already-spent ordinary behavior budget are not replayed. The virtual START was not itself a combat turn or resource-refresh event.

For Illusive Commands, an independently valid soft movement/interaction component that survives a blocked hard Action component establishes a new instruction and replaces the prior pending same-spell record. A saved-against, wholly invalid or wholly blocked instruction establishes no replacement.

A Dire Charm application keeps its repeat saves while at least one of its original components remains. Once it has none, its save schedule stops; an old save never removes a later application's replacement component. No hard-control history is refunded.

Command's Grovel does not inherently consume the ordinary Action. Its required Prone posture can coexist with another legal Action. Confusing Flash's Attack branch continues to spend the ordinary Action on exactly one ordinary attack.

## Root, physical restraints and suppression

Root supplies Speed0 only; it does not inherently apply Restrained, Grappled, Incapacitated, Action/Reaction loss or a teleport ban. A Speed0 source not named Root receives no invented Root identity. Multiple zero records coexist; ending one does not end another.

Printed restraint saves, escape Actions, size/anatomy limits, concentration and relationship endpoints win. **NEW fallback only** for genuine physical Restrained with no explicit escape, no sufficient fixed endpoint and no special-cure requirement: Action STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against recorded applying DC, otherwise10, ends **one selected** record on success. An adjacent helper may instead use Action STR(Athletics). None of the supplied active restraints needs this fallback. A fixed endpoint alone excludes it. No generic cutting, helper or object-HP escape is added to magical-only restraints.

Net Bolt retains printed Action STR(Athletics) escape, net AC10/HP5, maximum3 rounds and Huge+ -10 replacement. Tinker Net Trap retains its printed repeat save/Action escape. Earthen Grip's grounded-target requirement is an application requirement; the source does not say moving/teleporting away ends it. It persists after a legal teleport until concentration, printed time or its Action escape ends it. Tyrant's Impale and Panther retain their explicit reach/separation/reversion relationship endings. If suppression permits escape beyond a required maintained reach, the source ends and cannot resume. An attached physical net otherwise persists through suppression and can resume until removed/destroyed/expired.

Immunity suppresses only covered components; clocks and relationship checks continue. Word of Binding's Silenced and Speed0 are independent for immunity, while its successful repeat save ends both. A suppressed record does not grant active eligibility hooks. Ending one restriction does not cure unrelated damage, marks or components on the same card.

## Material identity, consumption and substitution

Keep the exact recipe ID and component occurrence. Global material names alone are insufficient: 143 embedded names have different tier/price/weight variants. Record identity as the recipe component's name, tier, category, properties, unit weight, unit value and source occurrence. Quantity belongs to the inventory lot, not the identity. Preserve component IDs where supplied; none are silently merged or normalized to a cheaper same-name material. The 2-gp crafting Crystal Vial and 5-gp equipment Vial remain distinct records unless an explicit compatibility/substitution ruling is recorded.

An exact recipe component's stored numeric `tier` remains part of that component's identity and may be compared for that recipe's explicit substitution requirements even when the stored number exceeds 6. This does not extend the generic V4 material-tier ladder or generic harvesting entitlement beyond Tier VI. A Tier 7–10 stored component therefore receives no generic harvest DC, public availability, rarity right or substitution source merely from that number; it requires its actual recipe/source acquisition procedure or another separately reviewed rule.

**Source:** substitutions require the relevant properties and tier unless the recipe names an irreplaceable ingredient. **Completion:** before spending materials, a substitute must satisfy each replaced unit's tier (equal or higher), all required functional properties and role, compatible physical form, and at least its required amount. The Director records the mapping and its actual unit quantities/weights/value. Higher price alone is not compatibility; a higher-tier component does not increase the result tier, quantity or effect. A unique named core cannot be replaced under this general permission. Do not repeatedly change the substitution after observing the outcome.

Reserve consumed quantities at the start and deduct them once at resolution or deliberate abandonment. Abandonment after work starts loses consumed inputs with no product/recovery roll; actual nonconsumed tools and intact independently stored unused supplies remain. Ingredients left outside the reservation remain usable but cannot also fund another order. Return only the exact quantities authorized by Masterwork or ordinary failure, never both for one result. No recovery from a Mishap. Component `consumed=false` returns its full reserved quantity; role=tool is not itself a consumed flag.

Nineteen source component rows have role=tool and consumed=true. Treat these as incorporated parts in those exact recipes, not the separately required reusable toolkit; retain their flags until individual recipe review. A focusing lens incorporated into a device is not a reusable station lens. The work order must supply both if it needs both. Never 'repair' all role=tool rows to nonconsumed in bulk.

Ordinary failure recovery uses each identity's physical units: an indivisible organ, lens, bottle or crystal rounds down to whole units; explicitly divisible bulk reagent can be recorded to 0.01 source units. Recovery never creates money. For example, four ordinary indivisible non-catalyst vials return one; one irreplaceable catalyst returns zero. These recovered lots retain their age and identity. A failed batch cannot be salvaged again for another automatic 25%.
